checks: Read s360_q28_twophase.py and the 7 output files; re-read the reported numbers (chi2 8.7/6.4 vs 157/177 and 52/29, lnBF 67/79 and 16.8/6.9, compact 0.5"/0.3", P(Tk_E>50)=0.999, Sigma_gas, X(HCO+) needed) and they match the logs and report.json. I did not re-run the grid, but the script logic matches what the summary describes.

The two-phase chi2 of 8.7/6.4 comes from 14 data points (12 fluxes + 2 one-sided floors) and about 9 free parameters (Tk,n,N,A for each phase, plus size). That is roughly 5 effective dof, so a good chi2 is nearly guaranteed. It is not evidence that the physical picture is right. The model is only compared with models that are structurally unable to fit, and the Occam factors (lnBF 5-80) are dominated by that.

Beam overlap not modelled. The 10" ladders are Gaussian-smoothed at the N_pos and S_pos positions, and N and S are only ~5" apart. So each 10" beam contains the other nucleus and the bridge. The model assumes the 10" flux at N is N's compact core plus an 'extended phase that fills every beam', and the same for S, independently. The 10" data at N and S are close to identical (HCN 2-1 12.4 vs 11.7, 3-2 4.8 vs 4.3 K km/s). So the findings 'extended A equal at N and S', 'extended Tk 112 K at both' and 'extended phase carries 75-90% of the 10" flux' are largely built in. The 'N/S contrast sits in the compact A' conclusion follows from the same construction. This was raised in the Q3 review (turn 009) and is not applied here.

The extended phase is constrained by only 3 lines per species at 10", with tau<=1 and filling 1 imposed and a grid with 1-2 populated points (Tk 112 K, n 3e4, N 3e13, log A 0.5 as a single grid point). P(Tk_E>50)>=0.99 is therefore a statement about the prior and grid. A thin ladder has the Tk-n degeneracy, and the 10" 2-1/3-2/4-3 ratios cannot fix Tk independently of n. The claim 'Q40 Tk>50 K is not a mixing artefact' is too strong.

The model treats the 0.24" T_b (N HCN 2.65 K, S 1.18 K) as a one-sided floor (>=0.85 Tb). These are measurements. A 0.3-0.5" source with T_R~3 K intrinsic is just consistent, but compact solutions with Tk 300 K and thick lines (best N fit: Tk 300, logN 15.5) predict T_b at 0.24" far above the observation, and nothing penalises this. The floors can only exclude cold or dilute solutions. Using them as two-sided (with a clumping/filling factor, or at least an upper bound from the 0.24" peak) is what actually constrains Tk_C and size.

Dust-bound tension: the extended thin phase carries 80% of the mass and needs X(HCO+)>=1-2e-8 (5-10e-8 for Td=100 K), above the usual range. This tension is a diagnostic that the extended-phase column (set by tau<=1 and filling 1 at 3e13) or the model is wrong; the summary leaves it open instead of testing it (filling<1 or lower N for the extended phase).

Compact Tk is declared unconstrained (P(Tk<=30)=0.18-0.78 vs prior 0.33). The S 'cool core allowed, mildly favoured (odds 1.3-3.6)' is below the level that supports a claim; call it consistent but untested. The question asked what Tk each component needs, and the honest answer is 'extended: degenerate with n; compact: not constrained', which the summary says only partly.

fixes.what: Model the N and S 10" beams jointly with beam overlap: predict the 10" flux at each position as the sum of N core, S core and a shared extended component convolved with the 10" Gaussian at the actual positions (N-S separation ~5", state it), and fit N and S together. Alternatively, drop the 10" data and use apertures at N/S at 2.2" or at least test the 10" ladder after subtracting the other nucleus's compact flux and the bridge.
fixes.why: Currently N and S 10" data are used as independent measures of independent 'extended phases'. At 5" separation they largely see the same gas, so equal extended Tk/A and the compact-only contrast are by construction.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Forward-model the beam: sum each component's brightness profile convolved with the beam centred on each position, with shared parameters for the common component, and report the extended-phase parameters once. Compare with a ladder at a resolution that separates N and S (taper to 3" or use 2.2" 1-0/3-2 plus 4-3 and 2-1 matched at 2.2").

fixes.what: Treat the 0.24" and 1.29" T_b as two-sided measurements (floor and ceiling, with a beam-filling/clumping factor as an explicit parameter), and show the best-fit compact solutions' predicted 0.24" T_b. Re-derive the compact Tk/size posterior.
fixes.why: One-sided floors let Tk=300 K thick solutions pass with a predicted T_b far above the observed 2.65 K; Tk_C is called 'unconstrained' partly because the measurement was not used as one.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Include the peak T_b at the native resolution as a data point with its error and model the source structure (Gaussian or clumps with filling factor f<1), then show which (theta,f,Tk) combinations survive.

fixes.what: Repeat the fit with a finer grid for the extended phase (Tk, n steps <=0.05-0.1 dex, free filling factor, tau<=1 relaxed to tau<=3) and report profile likelihoods in Tk_E and n_E rather than a posterior on 1-2 grid points. Show chi2(Tk_E) at fixed n.
fixes.why: P(Tk_E>50)>=0.99 is a grid/prior statement; the Tk-n degeneracy is not shown.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Profile the likelihood across Tk and n with the other parameters marginalised; quote the range excluded at delta chi2>4.

fixes.what: Report effective dof and a goodness-of-fit/null test: simulate data from the best one-state-two-size and two-phase models at the error model and see how often chi2 differences of the observed size arise; add a leave-one-out (drop 2.2" 1-0, drop 1.29", drop the floors) test of the two-phase result.
fixes.why: chi2 8.7/6.4 with ~5 dof and 9 parameters is not a test, and lnBF=5-80 relies on 10-15% errors with cross-project calibration. The S result (lnBF 4.6-12 vs one state) is not strong.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Parametric bootstrap and cross-validation; report which data drive the preference.

fixes.what: Resolve the dust tension: run the two-phase fit with the extended column capped by the dust bound for X(HCO+) in 1e-9..1e-8 and say whether the ladder still fits, and what happens to the extended Tk and n.
fixes.why: If the model needs X(HCO+)>1e-8, either the extended phase is not as described or the continuum bound is too low; the item should take a position.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Add the continuum-derived N(H2) as a constraint (Td range) in the joint fit; give gas mass fractions and the compact-phase mass and density (n x size) as derived quantities.

fixes.what: Derive and give the compact-phase quantities each interpretation predicts that can be tested (HCN 3-2/1-0 ratio and 4-3 at 0.5", H13CN 4-3 flux, HCN v2=1) for the Tk_C<=30 K and Tk_C>100 K solutions, and the compact-phase gas mass at X=1e-9..1e-8 (~100 pc).
fixes.why: Results are not carried to derived quantities that decide between the two Tk_C branches.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Tabulate predicted observables for the two branches and compare with existing data/limits, flagging which are decisive.

notes_for_questioner: Ask: with N and S only ~5" apart, which 10" ladder (or taper) is clean of the other nucleus? Can a matched 2.2" (or 3") 2-1/3-2/4-3 ladder be built at N and S to fit the extended phase independently of the cores? Can the 0.24" peak T_b be used with a filling-factor model to separate cool (S, Tk 20-30 K) from warm compact cores?
